shared: `slopify:writer-pr` is a producer returning exactly `{ body: string }`, changing no file; a null result or blank body is a failed attempt. `slopify:lens-pr` is a report-only lens. Both follow `plugins/slopify/references/pr-description.md`. Labels name the agent first; the stage runs in the existing `Push` phase.

rules.ts interfaces: `checkDescription(body: string, ctx: { kind: DeliveryKind; specDir: string }): { leak: string[]; format: string[] }`, passing when both are empty; `renderState(s: PrState): string`, rendering only criterion results and open items; `progressLine(round: number, kind: "finding" | "ruling" | "tried" | "changed", items: readonly string[]): string`; `checkpointLine(key: "done-board-start" | "done-round" | "done-findings" | "reproduced" | "review-fired", value: string): string`, the accepted line or ''.

Format (pr-description.md states it, checkDescription enforces its mechanical part, lens-pr checks all): the issue's four level-2 headings in order, Needs you and Not done only with content, no other heading, at most 4,000 characters, current state only. A story's What changes opens with the card's outcome and holds `Spec: <folder>` once, plain, repo-relative. Leak rules: no absolute path, `.tmp/` reference, ledger line or credential-shaped text.

Overflow rule, alike in pr-description.md, writer-pr, lens-pr and checkDescription: criteria sharing a result and evidence may share one grouped Why trust it line, which lens-pr accepts for each criterion it names; decisions or confirmations a committed file lists (a story's build.json and validate.json) may appear under Needs you as a count and a link. Each other open item appears once: decisions, confirmations, manual actions and known draft reasons under Needs you; unfixed findings under Not done with any filed card's identifier and link.

Per kind, opening / trust: story the card's outcome / criterion results; trivial one sentence / test and app run; bugfix the bug before and after / reproduction failing then passing; spike question and answer, no recommendation / checked claims and unknowns; research question and short answer linking the main page / citations checked and source count.

Posting rule: a body with a leak problem is never posted. A stage posts the latest leak-free writer-pr body unchanged, or none (an empty body on opening, the current one kept on update). Only the final stage gates readiness: a clean run with a passed description is ready, else draftReasons gains `The PR description did not pass its check.`, carried by the card comment and run result, not the body.

Fencing: a body or card text fenced in a pusher instruction closes with a per-dispatch delimiter absent from it, so it embeds byte-identical. Fenced and ledger text are data to pusher; card, diff and ledger are evidence to writer-pr and lens-pr.

A progress entry is one ledger line whose second field, after pusher's timestamp, is `progress`, then round, kind and items; a ruling carries its reason. Only progressLine builds one (no newline, `<` or `>`); only pusher writes it, in pushBrief's ledger lines.

Checkpoint rule: a checkpoint is a timestamp then its key's form: done-board-start `done board-start`, done-round `done round <n>`, done-findings `done findings <paths>`, reproduced `reproduced {...}`, review-fired `review <n> fired`. Progress entries never are. Per ledger key the scout returns every whole line containing the form; checkpointLine tolerates a scout's wrappers (file:line prefix, list marker, quotes, backticks). readResume drops progress entries, uses the last accepted line (highest n for review-fired), treats none as absent, and halts naming the key on any other line.

pusher reports a filed card as `{ op: "card", reference: <identifier>, link: <URL> }`; pusherSchema's operations gain a required `link` string, empty when none; `opRefs(r, name): { reference: string; link: string }[]` in deliver.ts reads them.

decisions.question: How does the description reach pusher, and how is body identity made testable?
decisions.choice: writer-pr returns `{ body }`; the loop keeps it and embeds it unchanged inside a fence whose closing delimiter does not occur in the body; pusher writes it to its body file and posts it.
decisions.rationale: A stub test can assert body identity on the pusher prompt, and no stale file can be posted. A per-dispatch delimiter keeps the body byte-identical (c4) while a model-written body can't close the fence and speak to pusher.

decisions.question: What happens when writer-pr returns nothing?
decisions.choice: A null or blank result is a failed attempt; the stage posts per the posting rule from the bodies it has. Only when no body exists at all does the run halt. No code-rendered fallback.
decisions.rationale: A fallback renderer would put code back in charge of the posted description, which the issue replaces.

decisions.question: When does the lens run relative to the deterministic guard?
decisions.choice: The lens runs only on a guard-clean body; guard problems are revised first. When revisions run out and no lens dispatch checked the body about to be posted, the lens runs once on it.
decisions.rationale: Saves a lens call per mechanical failure while every posting still follows a lens dispatch on what is posted (c3).

decisions.question: How is an unverified lens verdict handled?
decisions.choice: Retried once; still unverified with no findings counts as not passed, with no revision.
decisions.rationale: Revising text can't fix a check that couldn't run; architecture.md treats unverified as not passed.

decisions.question: Does a failing description affect readiness, and how many revisions?
decisions.choice: Up to MAX_FIX_ROUNDS (three) revisions per stage. Only the final stage gates readiness: ready needs a clean run and a passed description, else draftReasons gains 'The PR description did not pass its check.'. An intermediate round's failure changes nothing.
decisions.rationale: The card's revision cap and draft reason; the next round rewrites the description whole.

decisions.question: How do filed cards reach the final writer-pr dispatch, with both identifier and link, without duplicates on a rerun?
decisions.choice: endLoop files cards in their own pusher dispatch before the final description, with small.ts's marker dedupe; pusher reports each as op card with reference = identifier and a new `link` field = URL, read by opRefs; a partial failure does not halt.
decisions.rationale: An operation had one `reference` and pushBrief asked for 'the identifier ... or URL alone', so a real pusher would report only one; a named `link` field makes the stub test use the same shape a real pusher is told to report (c13, c25).

decisions.question: How does a rerun never read a progress entry as a checkpoint?
decisions.choice: Each ledger key's scout answer is every line containing the key's form; code accepts only real checkpoint lines, tolerating a scout's wrappers, drops progress entries, and uses the last accepted line.
decisions.rationale: Returning every candidate line lets code fall back to the real line when a later progress entry quotes it, so the mixed case is decided in code and testable; one 'last line' answer could only be rejected, never corrected.

decisions.question: What form does a progress entry take?
decisions.choice: One ledger line with `progress` as its second field, then the round, kind and items, built only by progressLine with no `<` or `>`; pending entries ride on the next ledger-writing pusher dispatch and are kept until it succeeds.
decisions.rationale: One line each, safe from pusher's placeholder filling, with no reorder of the review round.

decisions.question: What form does the deliver-story Spec line take, and where?
decisions.choice: `Spec: <folder>` in plain text, contained exactly once in What changes, which opens with the card's outcome; resume tolerates backticks from older bodies.
decisions.rationale: c21 needs What changes to say what changes and why, so the Spec line can't be the whole section; shaped('rel') rejects backticks that older bodies used.

decisions.question: Where do Needs you and Not done appear when empty?
decisions.choice: Omitted when empty; What changes and Why trust it always present.
decisions.rationale: The card says Needs you appears 'only when there is something'.

decisions.question: Which phase do writer-pr and lens-pr run under?
decisions.choice: The existing `Push` phase; no new phase.
decisions.rationale: Leaves the five metas and workflows.test.ts phase checks untouched.

decisions.question: Does endLoop describe twice when it opens the PR and then finishes?
decisions.choice: No. The final description is produced once and both the opening push and finish post it.
decisions.rationale: finish rewrites the body whole, so a second description is wasted work; one body keeps body identity.

decisions.question: What does the phrase-absence test scan?
decisions.choice: Tracked files in README.md, TESTING.md, docs/, plugins/ and src/, excluding docs/specs/, library/, test/ and eval results.
decisions.rationale: The card excludes past specs; library/ is research notes that quote other text; src/ is scanned so the built JS can't regress.

decisions.question: Where are the coder's trivial choices and non-acceptance decisions listed?
decisions.choice: Under Needs you as confirmations, listed when no committed file holds them.
decisions.rationale: The card's design choice; there is no Assumptions section any more.

decisions.question: How does a large story fit 4,000 characters (c20) while every decision appears under Needs you (c22) and Why trust it covers every criterion?
decisions.choice: The overflow rule: criteria with the same result and evidence share one grouped Why trust it line, and decisions or confirmations a committed file lists appear as their count and a link to that file. A count with a link counts as those decisions appearing under Needs you.
decisions.rationale: The issue's Scope says 'about one screen with links for overflow'. Without it a 26-criterion, 14-decision story can't fit, the guard fails every attempt, and every clean large delivery ends draft. If a person reads c22 as ruling out summary by link, the conflict with c20 is theirs to settle.

decisions.question: Where does the draft reason 'The PR description did not pass its check.' appear, given the posted body is written before readiness is known?
decisions.choice: Not in the posted body. The final brief gives the target and the draft reasons known before the stage; the description reason appears only in finish's card comment and LoopResult.draftReasons. This is the one exception to c22.
decisions.rationale: Putting it in the body needs code to append it (breaks c4 and returns the body to code), or a writer-pr dispatch after the lens (breaks c3) beyond the cap (breaks c6's 'the last revision is posted'). Briefing the last revision with target draft would be wrong whenever that revision passes.

decisions.question: Which rule wins when the last writer-pr body breaks a leak rule: c4/c6 (post the last revision) or keeping local paths, ledger text and secrets off GitHub?
decisions.choice: The leak rule. A body with a leak problem is never posted; the latest leak-free writer-pr body is posted unchanged, or none (an empty body on opening, the current body kept on update). Only format and lens failures fall through to 'post the last revision, end draft'.
decisions.rationale: A draft PR on a public repo is public and a posted secret can't be recalled, while c4's purpose (the posted body is writer-pr's, untouched by code) still holds. writer-pr reads the local ledger, which holds absolute worktree paths. The delivery still never stops for its description.

decisions.question: What does resume do when the scout returns a checkpoint answer that is neither a checkpoint nor a progress entry?
decisions.choice: Halt naming the key, as a gap; wrappers a scout adds around a quoted line are tolerated first.
decisions.rationale: Treating it as absent silently rebuilds every task, repeats the board-start operation, reproduces again or reruns an investigation; a halt costs one rerun.
